image.alt: Can Monsoon Infections Make Diabetes Harder to Control?

html:
Monsoon brings relief from the heat, but it also brings a higher risk of several infections. For people living with diabetes, an infection can be more than an uncomfortable few days. It may also make blood sugar harder to manage.

If your glucose readings suddenly start climbing while you have a fever, cough, stomach infection, or urinary infection, it is worth paying attention rather than assuming it is simply a bad reading. A diabetes specialist in Ahmedabad can help you understand what is happening and whether your diabetes treatment needs closer monitoring.

Why Can an Infection Raise Blood Sugar?

When you become ill, your body releases stress hormones to help fight the infection. These hormones can also raise blood glucose levels. At the same time, diabetes can make it harder for the body to fight certain infections and recover from them.

This can create a difficult cycle: the infection affects your blood sugar, while persistently high blood sugar can make it harder for your body to deal with the infection.

During the monsoon, infections linked to contaminated water and flooding also deserve attention. Leptospirosis, for example, can spread through contact with contaminated floodwater and can become serious if left untreated. People with diabetes should take particular care of their feet and any cuts or wounds after exposure to floodwater.

What Should You Do If You Fall Sick?

If you have diabetes and develop an infection during the monsoon:

  1. Check your blood sugar regularly. Illness can cause unexpected changes, even if your usual readings are stable.
  2. Stay hydrated. Fever, vomiting or diarrhoea can increase the risk of dehydration.
  3. Do not stop or change your diabetes medicines on your own. Speak to your doctor about what to do during illness.
  4. Keep an eye on wounds and your feet. Redness, swelling, pain, or a wound that is not healing should not be ignored.
  5. Seek medical advice if symptoms worsen. Persistent fever, difficulty breathing, repeated vomiting, or very high blood sugar may need urgent assessment.

When Should You See a Doctor?

A monsoon infection should not be brushed aside simply because it started as a mild fever or cough. If you have diabetes and your blood sugar becomes difficult to control while you are unwell, speak to a diabetes specialist in Ahmedabad for appropriate advice.
